research_question: Can RAKL detect weaknesses that are not reliably exposed by generic same-context self-reflection, while avoiding unsupported global self-knowledge claims and unnecessary reflection cost?
scope: support-only metacognitive audit classification; no promotion, routing, Constitution, or scientific-authority mutation
design_principles: self-reported confidence is evidence to calibrate, not authority
metacognitive competence is domain-scoped unless transfer is measured
reconstruction of an explanation can expose missing causal/mechanistic elements hidden by verbal familiarity
explicit countermodel generation is stronger than generic instructions to be unbiased
same-context self-review is not independent review
repeated unclassified residuals can indicate an ontology gap
target unreachability that cannot be resolved by the incumbent operator basis can indicate a missing method operator
reflection is triggered by registered signals rather than applied continuously
feedback-driven calibration change alone does not establish underlying capability improvement
missing external outcome evidence yields CANNOT_CHECK

primary_source_projections.projection: people can diagnose bias more readily in others than in themselves; introspection alone is an unreliable debiasing authority
people can overestimate explanatory understanding until required to produce a mechanistic explanation
explicitly considering the opposite can correct judgment more effectively than generic instructions to be unbiased
self-explanation can improve learning and problem solving by making inferential structure explicit
an outside/self-distanced perspective can reduce self-other asymmetry in wise reasoning
feedback can improve confidence calibration and response strategy without improving metacognitive sensitivity
requiring confidence reports can sometimes reduce response and change-of-mind accuracy, motivating selective rather than continuous reflection
LLM self-knowledge is domain-specific and does not reliably translate into action; external metacognitive control substantially reduces confident failures in the reported benchmark

worlds.falsifier: classifier launches a metacognitive audit merely because reflection is available
classifier invents a new ontology/operator gap instead of reopening the known fiber
one unclassified error is promoted directly to a missing-ontology claim
repeated residuals outside the incumbent taxonomy are silently forced into an existing fiber
system keeps retrying existing operators or claims the missing operator already exists
surface fluency is accepted as complete mechanistic understanding
generic be-unbiased language is counted as a successful countermodel challenge
same-context reviewer is credited as independent metacognitive evidence
calibration measured in one fiber is globalized to another fiber
system performs costly reflection despite no registered high-value trigger
improved calibration alone is represented as improved underlying task capability
self-report substitutes for missing external correctness evidence
system invents a new operator when a known unresolved operator/fiber already covers the gap
clean audit must not manufacture a weakness simply to appear reflective

blocking_invariants: the audit cannot mint scientific truth, mechanism authority, or method promotion
unknown-operator hypotheses remain candidates until separately benchmarked
self-reported confidence cannot override external outcome evidence
domain-specific calibration cannot be silently generalized
same-context reflection cannot count as independent review
generic reflection cannot erase immutable negative history
headline_null: If structured metacognitive audits do not discover held-out missing operator/ontology classes better than ordinary same-context reflection under matched cost, this layer remains an explanatory paper construct and should not add runtime complexity.
